en.title: GTA 6 Voice Actor Details 'Humongous' NDA, Calls Rockstar 'Crazy Secretive'
en.summary: A voice actor for the highly anticipated **Grand Theft Auto VI** has lifted the lid on Rockstar Games' famously tight-lipped development process. She described the non-disclosure agreement she signed as incredibly extensive, comparing it to the paperwork involved in major life purchases.
en.body:
The veil of secrecy surrounding **Grand Theft Auto VI** is legendary, and one of its voice actors has just given fans a rare glimpse behind the curtain. **Issa Lopez**, who lends her voice to a radio host on the fictional **Cocoteo FM** station, revealed the sheer scale of the non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before stepping into the recording booth.

Describing Rockstar's approach as "crazy secretive," Lopez compared the NDA to the mountain of paperwork required when purchasing a house or a car. "Have you ever signed papers to buy a house? To buy a car? You know, it’s thick! It was a pretty humongous pack of papers that came with it," she told Page Six in a recent interview. This level of confidentiality underscores the immense value placed on keeping **GTA 6**’s secrets under wraps until Rockstar is ready to reveal them.

## The Intense Recording Process

Lopez's experience highlights the pressure cooker environment of **GTA 6**'s development. Unlike typical voiceover gigs where actors receive scripts well in advance, she was essentially handed her lines on the spot. "In my usual voiceover gigs — let’s say you want me to do a commercial for you. I get a Zoom [link] maybe the day before, maybe the same day I get the script," she explained. For **GTA 6**, however, the process was immediate: "Everything was like, popped up on the screen. It was mad cool. It was like, ‘You ready? And I’m like, ‘Uh-huh.’ You press a button and then boop, it pops on the screen, they say hello, and there’s a bunch of people in your ear. And they’re like, ‘Okay, here it is,’ and that’s when you see it. You are put on the spot. And you better bring it."

## Fan Anticipation Reaches Fever Pitch

For fans eagerly awaiting **Grand Theft Auto VI**, these details only fuel the fire of anticipation. The sheer dedication to secrecy from Rockstar Games, extending to every individual involved in the project, speaks volumes about the scale and ambition of **GTA 6**. While some might find the NDA process daunting, Lopez herself found it "worth it," especially considering she didn't have to wait as long as many others who have reportedly been involved for over a decade. This intense preparation and secrecy suggest that Rockstar is aiming for a truly groundbreaking experience, one that they are meticulously guarding until its eventual release.

## What's Next

While specific release dates for **GTA 6** remain under wraps, the insights from **Issa Lopez** suggest that development is progressing, and the game is being protected with extreme diligence. Fans will be watching closely for any official announcements from Rockstar Games regarding further details or a release window.

content_raw: A voice actor who appeared in GTA 6 described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game, calling the project “crazy secretive.” Issa Lopez is a voice actor who plays a radio host on GTA 6’s fictional Cocoteo FM radio station, a Latin channel that plays reggaeton and dembow tracks featuring Spanish-speaking artists from the Caribbean and Latin America. In a November 20 interview with Page Six , Lopez revealed that she recorded her lines for the station as recently as September 2026, and said the NDA she was made to sign before officially performing the part was comparable to the process of purchasing a home or a vehicle. “Have you ever signed papers to buy a house? To buy a car? You know, it’s thick! It was a pretty humongous pack of papers that came with it. But I mean, it’s worth it! And I didn’t have to wait like all these other folks. Some of these folks have been working on this for like 10–11 years, you know what I mean?” she said. She went on to describe the recording process for her lines, saying that she hadn’t seen anything until the day of the performance. With no time to prepare, she was essentially “put on the spot” — but she was so excited about the opportunity that she didn’t mind. “In my usual voiceover gigs — let’s say you want me to do a commercial for you. I get a Zoom [link] maybe the day before, maybe the same day I get the script,” she explained. “Everything was like, popped up on the screen. It was mad cool. It was like, ‘You ready? And I’m like, ‘Uh-huh.’ You press a button and then boop, it pops on the screen, they say hello, and there’s a bunch of people in your ear. And they’re like, ‘Okay, here it is,’ and that’s when you see it. You are put on the spot. And you better bring it. And after that, I don’t know — whatever was in front of my face disappeared. “ Lopez revealed that she wasn’t told what the project was for, but figured it out based on context clues from an email titled “heard by millions,” saying she “read it and knew what it was for.” She also didn’t know that Bad Bunny would be co-hosting the Cocoteo station alongside her, leading to a wild realization once Rockstar released the radio stations before the game actually came out. “We knew nothing. I saw the liners, and when I saw the liners I was like, ‘Okay, I know why I got the gig.’ ‘Cause it was like Puerto Rican dot com. It was super easy. But it was so cool, because Rockstar let me be myself. …they were like, ‘Issa, we want natural. Whatever you got, we want,'" she said. The actors in GTA 6 were extremely secretive about their involvement in the project. Most notably, actress Manni L. Perez, who plays Lucia, was under immense pressure after fans sleuthed her social media accounts and figured out it was her before she could officially reveal the information. Now, she’s up for best performance at The Game Awards, which is one of eight nominations the game has secured mere weeks before the show takes place this December. O
